blocking.section: Multi-region; Cells and blast radius > Failure containment; High availability > Ruralz Control availability
blocking.issue: Losing the home Region also takes down Ruralz Control for every Region, and the document never models that combination. The surviving Region has to absorb the lost Region's traffic at the same moment it cannot enroll a single new Node. The 30% headroom rule cannot cover that. The failure table treats Region loss and Ruralz Control loss as separate, independent rows. Hidden single point of failure: all Raft voters sit in one Region.
blocking.evidence: Line 208: "Voters SHOULD share one Region". Figure 4, line 389: "Ruralz Control: three Raft voters" only in eu-west-1. Line 175: "New Nodes without Last-Known-Good stay not ready until they enroll (pack 8.11), so an autoscaler adds no capacity during a long outage. Clusters SHOULD keep 30% headroom above peak (target)". Line 531: "| Region lost | Its Cells; survivors count alone, up to R × each limit |". Line 530: "| Ruralz Control down or quorum lost | Management of every Cell it serves; no request errors |". Line 428: the Divided pattern gives prod-us a 40% share.
blocking.fix: Failure scenario: active-active eu-west-1 and us-east-1 at 50/50, and eu-west-1 is lost. All three voters go with it, so Enrollment stops in every Region (RZ-CP-004). Geo DNS moves 100% of traffic to us-east-1, which is sized with 30% headroom and needs 100%. The autoscaler adds pods that stay not ready. Kubernetes pods rescheduled with an emptyDir ${RURALZ_DATA_DIR} lose their identity and Last-Known-Good and cannot return either, so capacity shrinks. Consumers on the Divided pattern are capped at their 40% share while they carry 100% of their traffic. Fix: (1) Add a 'Home Region lost' row to Failure containment covering both effects. (2) Size active-active Regions for R/(R-1) of peak each (target), or state that a Region-loss plan requires pre-provisioned Nodes. (3) Require ${RURALZ_DATA_DIR} on persistent storage wherever Nodes may be rescheduled during an outage, or state the capacity loss and extend OQ-scalability-and-distributed-state-7. (4) Name the DR path: restore the Control Store from `ruralz control backup` in another Region, owned by High availability and disaster recovery. (5) State what Divided shares do on Region loss. (6) Add a chaos experiment 'home Region lost', Planned (M4), whose pass criteria include surviving-Region capacity.

blocking.section: Distributed state catalog (Published Node count row); Chaos experiments (CE-10); Limits and bottlenecks > Cell and Cluster bottlenecks
blocking.issue: The document does not define the published Node count while Ruralz Control rebuilds it after a replica restart, a leader failover or a replica loss. Control plane and GitOps qualifies Nodes by 10 minutes of connection and publishes large decreases at once. After a reconnect storm, the published count can therefore collapse. A collapsed count sends derived ceilings toward the full limit and multiplies hot-key GCRA traffic. That puts Ruralz Control indirectly on the request path through shard saturation, which contradicts SG-1 and the claim of 'no request errors'. There is also no N+1 rule for replicas: the 10,000-Node target equals the capacity of exactly two replicas.
blocking.evidence: Line 238: "| Published Node count | Control Store, sent in HeartbeatReply | Lagging: 10-minute qualification, increases at most 10% per minute (target) |". 04 line 115: "clusterNodeCount counts ready Nodes that ACKed a Revision and stayed connected 10 minutes (target); large decreases publish at once". 04 line 484: "Heartbeat aggregates, stream state | Memory; rebuilt by resync". Line 590: "| CE-10 | Every Ruralz Control replica restarted at once | All Nodes reconnect within 5 minutes (target), within stream admission rates |". Line 159: "each serves about 5,000 streams ... a deployment targets 10,000 Nodes (target) ... Voters stay at three or five."
blocking.fix: Failure scenario: 1,000 Nodes, and every replica restarts (CE-10), or one of three replicas is lost at 10,000 Nodes. Every reconnected stream has been connected for less than 10 minutes, so the rebuilt count qualifies few Nodes, and the decrease publishes at once. With N_published near 0, each derived ceiling becomes about the full limit. A hot key then reaches GCRA up to N_serving / N_published times as often, pushes its shard past about 100,000 calls per second (hypothesis), and opens every Node's breaker for that shard. Co-tenant closed Token Budgets return RZ-STS-003. Recovery takes 10 minutes plus about ln(N)/ln(1.1) minutes. Fix: (1) Specify that the count never decreases because Ruralz Control restarted, failed over or lost streams. Only qualified Nodes that miss three heartbeats reduce it, and qualification survives a reconnect to another replica because it is keyed by node.id in committed state. (2) Add that rule to the catalog row. (3) Add pass criteria to CE-10 and CE-7: the published count drops by no more than 10% (target), and no State client breaker opens. (4) Add a sizing rule: at least ceil(N / 5,000) + 1 replicas across zones (hypothesis).

blocking.section: Distributed state catalog > Distributed rate limits (Hot keys); Cells and blast radius > Failure containment; Chaos experiments (CE-12)
blocking.issue: The hot-key mitigation is wrong for a key whose admitted rate, not only its offered rate, exceeds one shard. Every locally admitted request runs GCRA, and N × ceiling is at least the limit, so a declared ceiling cannot cut calls below the limit. CE-12 passes while the shard is saturated. The blast-radius row also leaves out the co-tenant closed Policies on that shard.
blocking.evidence: Line 289: "A constant key above one shard's capacity, about 100,000 script calls per second (hypothesis), needs a declared ceiling or local-only enforcement (OQ-traffic-management-and-resilience-1)." Line 161: "A hot key cannot be split; it is bounded locally". Line 529: "| Hot key | One shard of one Cell |". Line 586: "| CE-12 | Hot key at 10 times one shard's capacity | Calls for it at most N × ceiling per window | Planned (M1) |".
blocking.fix: Failure scenario: a service-wide ratelimit with constant key and {requests: 300000, window: 1s} protects an Upstream, and 300,000 requests per second arrive. Every request passes its local bucket and runs one EVALSHA, which is 3x shard capacity. All Nodes' breakers for that shard open, the limit fails open, and every other key on the shard applies failureMode, including ai.token-budget (503). CE-12 still passes because N × ceiling is not exceeded. Fix: (1) State the bound: GCRA calls per key are at most min(offered, N × ceiling) and at least the admitted rate. (2) State that a key whose requests per window exceeds 50% of one shard's call capacity (hypothesis) MUST use local-only enforcement, and add an Open question for a validation warning (configuration-model). (3) Rewrite the Failure containment row to include co-tenant closed Policies on the shard. (4) Give CE-12 a pass criterion on shard health: shard script CPU under 70% (target) and no co-tenant breaker opens.

blocking.section: High availability > State Store availability; Distributed state catalog > State client and RZ-STS error codes; Chaos experiments (CE-5)
blocking.issue: The State Store failover path can trigger a reconnect storm. No State client reconnect backoff, jitter or connect-rate bound is defined. Each Node re-runs SCRIPT LOAD on every connection, and half-open probes are spread over only ±20% of 1 s. At the Cell ceiling, the new primary receives 10,000 TLS connections at once. The failover window has no number, although Traffic management gives about 15 s (hypothesis). CE-5 does not check reconnect load or the length of that window.
blocking.evidence: Line 220: "| SCRIPT LOAD at connect, reconnect and failover | MUST (Node) |". Line 330: "Per Node it keeps 2 pipelined connections per shard plus up to 8 dedicated ones ... half-opens after 1 s ± 20% and closes after 3 successes (target)". Line 567: "| Connections per shard | 10 × N_serving, 10,000 at 1,000 Nodes (hypothesis) | Refused connections | Raise the server limit |". Line 223: "the Cell applies failureMode until the new primary answers". Line 584: "| CE-5 | State Store primary killed | Extra admissions within the lag bound; never two round trips per Policy |". 09 line 490: "about 15 s of failover (hypothesis) gets failureMode".
blocking.fix: Failure scenario: a 1,000-Node Cell loses a shard primary. Within about 400 ms every Node redials, which means 10,000 TLS handshakes, 1,000 sets of SCRIPT LOAD, and half-open probes, all against a replica that is still promoting. Refused or slow connects keep breakers open, so the failover window stretches past 15 s. Closed Token Budgets return 503 for that whole window, with no stated bound. Fix: (1) Specify State client reconnects with exponential backoff and full jitter, for example base 100 ms and cap 5 s (target), plus a per-Node connect rate. (2) Spread half-open probes over 1 to 3 s (target). (3) Open the 8 dedicated connections lazily. (4) State the failover-window bound (about 15 s (hypothesis), matching 09) and its effect on each Policy type. (5) Give CE-5 a Node count of at least 100 (target) and pass criteria: every Node reconnected within 10 s (target) and a failureMode window of at most 15 s (target).

blocking.section: Consistency and accuracy bounds
blocking.issue: The derived-ceiling fail-open bound leaves out the one-token-per-Node floor that Traffic management and resilience applies. At 10x to 100x Node counts with small limits, the real admission is many times the stated bound. CE-4's pass criterion uses the floored ceiling of 10, so it is looser still and would pass a regression.
blocking.evidence: Line 353: "| Rate Limit, fail-open | Derived ceiling, OQ-traffic-management-and-resilience-16 option (b) | At most N_serving / N_published × 2 × requests per aligned window (target) |". 09 line 264: "each derived-ceiling bucket holds max(1, 2 × requests / N_published) tokens per epoch-aligned window". 09 line 479: "one token per Node at least". Line 583: "| CE-4 | ... | Per key at most N_serving × ceiling per window".
blocking.fix: Failure scenario: {requests: 10, window: 1s} on 1,000 Nodes with the State Store black-holed. The stated bound is 20 per second. 09 admits max(1, 0.02) = 1 per Node, which is 1,000 per second, or 100x the limit. CE-4's 'N_serving × ceiling', with the derived ceiling floored at 10, would accept 10,000 per second. Fix: (1) Change the row to 'At most N_serving × max(1, 2 × requests / N_published) per aligned window (target)'. (2) Add the 1,000-Node small-limit example. (3) Make CE-4 check that same expression for derived ceilings and N_serving × ceiling only for declared ceilings.

blocking.section: Consistency and accuracy bounds; Horizontal scaling > Warm-up; Chaos experiments (CE-8, CE-9)
blocking.issue: The bounds table gives no number for three cases that Traffic management quantifies: scale-out while the count lags, a count frozen by a Ruralz Control outage, and restarted Control-mode Nodes that have no count. The document owns these bounds (pack 8.8), yet CE-9 has no numeric pass criterion. CE-8 restarts Nodes during quorum loss, which creates Nodes without a count, but checks only readiness.
blocking.evidence: Line 570: "| Node-count lag | Plus 10% per minute (target) | Over-admission after scale-out | Declared ceilings |". Line 589: "| CE-9 | Scale from 10 to 100 Nodes in 2 minutes | Over-admission within the derived-ceiling bound | Planned (M2) |". Line 58: "Derived ceilings fall back to the full limit with a fail-open clamp and reason node_count_unknown" (no number). 09 line 493: "10 to 100 Nodes fail open at up to 20 × limit for about 34 minutes". 09 lines 494-495: "N_countless × the clamp ... 10 × limit (hypothesis)" and "N_serving / N_frozen × 2 × limit, 20 × limit after a 10 to 100 scale-out".
blocking.fix: Failure scenario: an autoscaler takes a Cluster from 10 to 100 Nodes during a State Store brownout, and the Rate Limit admits 20x its limit for about 34 minutes. The owning document states no such number, and CE-9 accepts any result. Fix: (1) Add rows for: scale-out lag, 'N_serving / N_published × 2 × requests, 20 × requests for about 34 minutes at 10 to 100 Nodes (hypothesis)'; a frozen count, 'N_serving / N_frozen × 2 × requests (hypothesis)'; and Control-mode Nodes without a count, 'N_countless × max(1, requests / 100) per window (target)'. (2) Put those numbers into the CE-9 pass criteria, and add an admission criterion to CE-8.

blocking.section: Distributed state catalog > Distributed rate limits; Consistency and accuracy bounds
blocking.issue: The document claims per-request GCRA keeps the Cell limit exact while the State Store is healthy. In the same section it recommends option (a) of OQ-traffic-management-and-resilience-20. Under that option, first-seen keys past the budget are admitted local-only, without GCRA, while the State Store is healthy. The healthy-State-Store rows have no bound for this case. Under a 10x key-rotation flood it is the dominant over-admission.
blocking.evidence: Line 287: "GCRA runs per admitted request ... keeping the Cell limit exact while the State Store is healthy." Line 291: "This document recommends option (b) of OQ-traffic-management-and-resilience-16, option (a) of -20 and option (c) of -19". Line 350: "| Rate Limit | Healthy State Store | At most requests per window sustained ...". 09 line 214: "past it, as OQ-traffic-management-and-resilience-20 proposes, a 10 s local-only entry (target) at the per-Node ceiling, capacity and refill alike, without GCRA."
blocking.fix: Failure scenario: a credential-stuffing flood rotates source.ip keys past B = 20,000 first-seen calls per second. Each new key is admitted local-only at up to N × ceiling per window for 10 s on a healthy State Store. With the floor of 10 on 1,000 Nodes, that is 10,000 per second per key against a 10-per-second limit. Fix: (1) Qualify the 'exact' claim. (2) Add a healthy-State-Store row: 'First-seen key past budget, OQ-traffic-management-and-resilience-20 option (a): at most N_serving × ceiling per window for 10 s (target)'. (3) Cite the first-seen call bound from 09.

blocking.section: Consistency and accuracy bounds (Token Budget rows); Chaos experiments (CE-13)
blocking.issue: The healthy closed Token Budget overshoot bound is narrower than the bound in AI/LLM gateway, which owns it and is a depends_on document. It drops the (attempts - 1) × R term per request and the hidden-reasoning term. Under Provider Fallback at scale, spend can exceed this document's number while staying within the owner's.
blocking.evidence: Line 359: "| Token Budget | Healthy, closed | Overshoot at most the sum of input-estimate errors, SM-10, owned by AI/LLM gateway (hypothesis) |". 06 line 326: "at most the sum of input-estimate errors across concurrent requests ... plus (attempts - 1) x R per concurrent request ... plus, while OQ-ai-llm-gateway-17 is open, hidden reasoning above C on gemini and ollama."
blocking.fix: Failure scenario: 200 concurrent streams using fallback with 3 candidates. A provider brownout produces extra attempts, each of which can consume up to R. Measured overshoot is 2 × R × 200, which violates this document's bound but is correct per 06, so CE-13 fails spuriously or is loosened ad hoc. Fix: quote 06's full bound in the row, citing the owner, and use the same bound in the CE-13 pass criterion.

blocking.section: Distributed state catalog > Post-commit write queue
blocking.issue: Draining the classes strictly in table order puts cache invalidations behind cache stores and Plugin writes behind everything else. Under sustained 10x store load, the 6,400-item invalidation class fills and drops. That defeats the reserved slice Traffic management relies on, and Plugin writes can starve without limit.
blocking.evidence: Line 326: "Eight writers per Node drain the classes in table order, pipelining up to 64 writes per batch (target)." Line 323: "| Cache invalidations | 6,400 items, the reserved 10% (target) | One retry, then drop |". 09 line 380: "Generation bumps get a reserved 10% of that queue and one retry (target)". 09 line 388: "as invalidations must not drop".
blocking.fix: Failure scenario: a flash sale drives cache stores at the writers' full throughput. The 16,000 queued stores are always drained first, so invalidations wait, reach 6,400 and drop. Stale prices are then served for up to 25 h (target). Fix: (1) Drain invalidations first, or give each class a guaranteed writer share, for example 2 of the 8 writers for invalidations and settlements (target). (2) Bound the maximum queueing delay per class (target). (3) Add a chaos or benchmark case with store saturation plus invalidations.

blocking.section: Distributed state catalog > Post-commit write queue; Limits and bottlenecks > Per-Node limits
blocking.issue: The Plugin-writes class has an item cap but no byte cap. Neither this document nor WASM plugin system caps the size of a value (only keys, at 256 bytes). The per-Node memory claim for caches and the queue is therefore false, and a per-Node structure is unbounded, which contradicts SG-7.
blocking.evidence: Line 324: "| Plugin writes | 9,600 items (target) | Drop per Plugin Policy |". Line 559: "these limits add at most 64 MiB for keys, 256 MiB for balancers and 128 MiB for caches and the queue (target)". 05 line 186: "Limits (target): 256-byte keys, ttlMillis 1 ms to 24 h, 10,000 keys per Policy per Node per minute, one onLog write per request".
blocking.fix: Failure scenario: a Plugin writes 1 MiB session blobs at onLog. 9,600 queued items hold about 9.4 GiB, which blows the 128 MiB claim, and the Node exceeds GOMEMLIMIT and is OOM-killed. Fix: (1) Give the Plugin-writes class a byte cap, for example 16 MiB (target). (2) Add an Open question to WASM plugin system for a per-value size cap. (3) Recompute the per-Node memory sum.

blocking.section: Horizontal scaling > Autoscaling signals; High availability > Ruralz Gateway availability
blocking.issue: Two capacity targets contradict each other. Autoscaling lets steady-state CPU sit just under 60%, while availability requires survivors to stay under 80% CPU after losing the largest zone. With two zones, a zone loss pushes survivors to about 120%. With three zones it pushes them to about 90%.
blocking.evidence: Line 141: "| CPU | Container CPU utilization | 60% over 2 minutes (target) |". Line 169: "A Cluster SHOULD run at least three Nodes in at least two zones (target), sized so that losing the largest zone keeps survivors under 80% CPU (target)."
blocking.fix: Failure scenario: three zones at 58% CPU, just under the scale-out trigger, and one zone is lost. Survivors reach 87% CPU and in-flight units saturate before the autoscaler reacts, so requests get 503 RZ-RT-005. Fix: derive the scale-out threshold from the zone count, as threshold = 80% × (Z - 1) / Z (target): 40% for two zones, about 53% for three. Alternatively, restrict the 60% figure to four or more zones and state the formula.

blocking.section: High availability > Ruralz Control availability (Figure 2)
blocking.issue: The required Raft HA state diagram models staleness as an alternative to candidacy, not as a timer that runs alongside it. A voter in a minority partition goes from Follower to Candidate and loops there. On this diagram it never becomes Stale and never sends Reconnect (rebalance). That contradicts the fencing rule in Control plane and GitOps, which applies to any replica without word from a leader. The 30 s threshold is also untagged.
blocking.evidence: Line 189: "Follower --> Candidate: no leader heartbeat within HeartbeatTimeout". Line 191: "Candidate --> Candidate: split vote or no majority, new election after ElectionTimeout". Line 194: "Follower --> Stale: leader contact lost for one election timeout". Line 196: "Stale --> Rebalancing: stale for 30 s". 04 line 492: "A replica without word from a leader for one election timeout (hypothesis) is stale ... After 30 s stale (target) it sends Reconnect (rebalance)."
blocking.fix: Failure scenario: a zone partition isolates one of three voters. It campaigns forever as Candidate, and its Nodes stay pinned to it without being told to rebalance to the healthy majority. They miss Rollouts and trust updates for the whole partition. Fix: (1) Model fencing as a separate concurrent region in the diagram (stateDiagram-v2 -- concurrency) or as a composite state entered from both Follower and Candidate. (2) Say that stale serving applies in Candidate too. (3) Tag the threshold: 'stale for 30 s (target)'.

blocking.section: Stateless data plane
blocking.issue: The inventory claims to be complete, but it leaves out per-Node state that this document and its dependencies create. Acceptance criterion 3 fails, as does the document's own rule that new per-Node state needs a row.
blocking.evidence: Line 50: "This table is the complete inventory of in-memory per-Node state; new per-Node state needs a row here before it ships." Missing: the State client's per-shard connections, breakers and 8,192 in-flight call slots (this document, line 330); the Response Cache revalidation queue of 256 entries and the miss-coalescing table of up to 4,096 keys (09 lines 394 and 396); the Vary-name LRU per URI (09 line 376); the per-shard INFO memory readings and per-shard store byte budgets c (09 lines 385-386); and the per-Node first-seen budget counter (09 line 214).
blocking.fix: Failure scenario: an operator sizing memory or reasoning about a Node kill uses this table as the complete list. The unlisted structures are bounded elsewhere but have no stated loss consequence here. After a restart, for example, the INFO memory reading is missing and stores run uncapped until the first read. Fix: add a row for each item above, with bound, rebuilt-from, and why losing it is safe. For the INFO memory reading, state that stores are skipped until the first read after start (target).

blocking.section: Distributed state catalog > State client and RZ-STS error codes
blocking.issue: The RZ-STS registry fixes every code at 503 before commit. Pack 8.10 and the Configuration model require 502 when a closed failure happens in a response Phase before commit. A Plugin Policy can make its one blocking State Store call in a response Phase.
blocking.evidence: Line 332: "All codes return 503 before commit in the Data plane format." Lines 336-340: every Status is "503". Pack 8.10: "| A response Phase before commit | Replace the response with 502 |". 02 line 385: "otherwise 503; 502 in a response Phase". 05 line 176: "state_get ... Before commit, never onChunk".
blocking.fix: Failure scenario: a plugin Policy in onUpstreamResponseHeaders calls state_get while the shard breaker is open. This document says 503 RZ-STS-003, while pack 8.10 requires 502, so implementations and tests diverge. Fix: change the Status column to '503 in a request Phase; 502 in a response Phase before commit (pack 8.10)' and reword line 332.

blocking.section: Multi-region > Regional versus global quotas
blocking.issue: The Divided Quota example puts a Bundle kind (Consumer) and control-plane-only kinds (Environment, Cluster) in one YAML stream with no file boundary. Loaded as one Bundle file, it fails with RZ-CFG-017.
blocking.evidence: Lines 434-476: one yaml fence holding kind: Consumer, then ---, kind: Environment (prod-eu), kind: Environment (prod-us) and kind: Cluster (prod-us-east). 02 line 594: "Environment and Cluster are rejected inside a Bundle (RZ-CFG-017) ... They live elsewhere, such as control/".
blocking.fix: Failure scenario: an operator copies the sketch into consumers.yaml and `ruralz bundle validate` fails with RZ-CFG-017. Fix: split it into two fences, each preceded by a sentence naming the path: the Consumer in the Bundle (for example consumers/partner-acme.yaml), and the Environments and Cluster under control/ outside the Bundle.

blocking.section: Cells and blast radius > Failure containment; Multi-region > Topologies
blocking.issue: The document says evacuating a Cell lets limits apply once per Cell only 'briefly'. Quota windows run up to 720 h, so a moved Consumer gets a fresh full allowance for the rest of the window, up to 30 days. Active-standby failover resets every counter. No number is given, and spend-bearing Token Budgets are affected the same way.
blocking.evidence: Line 534: "Receiving Cells start with empty counters for moved clients, so limits briefly apply once per Cell until old windows expire." Line 378: "| Active-standby | ... | Counters start empty after failover |". 09 line 328: "24h resets at midnight, 720h every 30 days".
blocking.fix: Failure scenario: a partner with a 3,000,000-per-720h Quota and a 2,000,000-per-24h token Token Budget is evacuated on day 2. Over the next 28 days it can consume up to 6,000,000 requests. The daily token budget doubles for the rest of that day, which is real provider spend. Fix: (1) Replace 'briefly' with the bound 'up to one extra limit per receiving Cell for the remainder of each open window, up to 720 h (target)'. (2) Add a row to the bounds table. (3) Recommend Region-pinned tenants or the Divided pattern for spend-bearing Quotas. (4) Add an Open question on carrying counters across an evacuation.

blocking.section: CLI command tree
blocking.issue: Revision prefix lookup has no REST path to call. The CLI accepts `rev-<12 hex>` as a lookup key for Revision sources, but the REST conventions allow only full digests in paths, and no collection filter or search parameter is defined. So the CLI cannot resolve a prefix, or detect that one is ambiguous, without listing every Revision, and that listing is unbounded.
blocking.evidence: "Read commands accept the display form `rev-<12 hex>` as a lookup key and fail with exit code 2 when it is ambiguous" (Bundle verbs in detail); "| Revision identifier | `rev-162af81f5de4` or `sha256:<64 hex>` | A Revision from Ruralz Control, fetched from `revisions` |"; versus REST conventions: "Digests in paths and bodies are full `sha256:<64 hex>` values"
blocking.fix: Add a lookup to the REST API table, for example `GET /api/v1/revisions?digestPrefix=<12 hex>&environment=NAME`, that returns at most 2 matches, and state that the CLI uses it. Add it as a proposal to OQ-cli-and-api-surface-3, or open a new Open question owned by control-plane-and-gitops. The other option is to require the full `sha256:<64 hex>` for every Revision source and change the worked example (`ruralz bundle diff rev-162af81f5de4 ...`) to match.

blocking.section: CLI command tree
blocking.issue: The document does not say how `ruralz test run --bundle` and `ruralz dev run` start a local `ruralzd` for an arbitrary Bundle. Listener ports are required Bundle fields and part of the digest (Configuration model Gateway: `port: 8443 # required`). The admin port defaults to 9901. The only process settings are `RURALZ_CONFIG`, `RURALZ_DATA_DIR` and `RURALZ_LOG_LEVEL`. So there is no way to move listeners to loopback or ephemeral ports without changing the tested Revision. Parallel CI jobs would collide on 8443 and 9901. The `secretRef` values, such as the `file` TLS certificates under `/etc/ruralz/tls`, would not resolve on a CI runner, so `/readyz` never turns 200. File-mode `ruralzd` applies no overlay (the OQ-configuration-model-10 decision), yet `dev run --env` promises Hot Reload of an overlaid render, and the re-render and watch loop is not described.
blocking.evidence: "With `--bundle DIR`, `ruralz test run` starts a local `ruralzd` on loopback ports with that Bundle rendered for `--env`"; "| `ruralz dev run` | Launch a local `ruralzd` on a Bundle directory with Hot Reload | `[DIR]`, `--env`, `--environments` | Local `ruralzd` |"
blocking.fix: Add a subsection, "Local ruralzd launched by the CLI", that states: (1) how listener and admin ports are rebound, either as a CLI-only render transform whose digest is reported as a test digest that differs from the Revision, or through a proposed `RURALZ_*` listener and admin override setting, recorded in a new OQ-cli-and-api-surface-N that needs a pack section 2 amendment; (2) how `secretRef` values are satisfied locally, for example a `--secret-overrides FILE` mapping, or a documented failure with RZ-CFG-026 and exit 2; (3) that the CLI waits for `/readyz` on the chosen admin port with a bounded timeout (target); (4) that `dev run --env` re-renders on change to a temporary rendered file, which it replaces atomically for Hot Reload.

blocking.section: CLI command tree
blocking.issue: The document does not say how `ruralz node drain` finds the process to signal. A file lock taken with flock has no queryable owner PID. System overview says the old process releases the lock at Drain start, so during a Zero-Downtime Upgrade the lock holder changes. The CLI and a containerized `ruralzd` usually live in different PID namespaces, and signaling another user's process needs privileges. The command table defines no PID source, and the text does not cover a lock that no process holds, or one that changes owner while `--timeout` waits.
blocking.evidence: "on the Node's host it sends SIGTERM to the `ruralzd` process holding the file lock on `${RURALZ_DATA_DIR}`, starting a Drain as a process manager would ([ADR-0015](...)), and waits for exit or `--timeout`"; the table lists only "`--data-dir PATH` (default `RURALZ_DATA_DIR`), `--timeout DURATION` | Local process signal"
blocking.fix: Specify the mechanism, for example a PID and start-time record that the lock holder writes under `${RURALZ_DATA_DIR}` (layout owned by Data plane). The CLI then verifies the record against the lock (for example a POSIX `F_OFD_GETLK` or `/proc/locks` check on Linux) before it signals. Define exit 2 for no holder, a stale record or permission denied, and state that the command signals only the process recorded at invocation. In Kubernetes or systemd, send operators to Pod deletion or `systemctl stop` instead. Record the Linux-only limit, and leave the remote case to OQ-cli-and-api-surface-4.

blocking.section: CLI command tree
blocking.issue: `ruralz control join` cannot be built as specified. Joining a replica needs a key pair on the new replica's host, a certificate stored in that replica's data directory, and a pinned server CA for the first TLS dial. The command has no data directory, no key or output location and no pin input, and the global `--ca-file` covers only 8090 and 9901. Security and identity describes `Join` as sent "from a replica without a peer certificate" over a pinned server CA, so it is not clear whether the CLI or the replica process dials 8092, or where the private key is created.
blocking.evidence: "| `ruralz control join` | Join a replica to the Raft cluster by redeeming a one-time `admin` token | `--peer HOST:8092`, `--token-file PATH` | Peer layer 8092 `Join` |"; Figure 3: "cli -.->|\"control join\"| peer"; Security and identity transport table: "except token `Join` from a replica without a peer certificate ... `Join` redeems a one-time `admin` token over a pinned server CA"
blocking.fix: Define `ruralz control join` as acting on the local replica's data directory: add a `--data-dir PATH` flag (required). The replica key is generated there, and the certificate chain and peer CA are written there. State that the join token embeds the SHA-256 fingerprint of the 8092 server CA, as Enrollment tokens do, and that the CLI refuses an unpinned dial. Alternatively, make `join` a mode of `ruralz control serve` (`-- --join HOST:8092 --join-token-file PATH`) and update Figure 3 and the Surface column.

blocking.section: CLI command tree
blocking.issue: `ruralz control restore` cannot run in the order given. It needs a root-signed anchor set with a new online key. That key's private half must already exist in the restored deployment when the offline root signs the set, but restore targets an empty deployment and has no input for the private key, and no step that generates it and exports its public half. The backup is also "encrypted and signed" (Control plane and GitOps), yet restore takes no decryption key. The Control Store data directory it writes to is not named either.
blocking.evidence: "| `ruralz control restore` | Restore a Control Store snapshot into an empty deployment | `FILE`, `--anchor-set PATH` (required), `--revocation-list PATH` | Local Control Store |" and "requires a root-signed anchor set so that the restored Ruralz Control opens a higher `storeEpoch` before any delivery"
blocking.fix: Make restore two-step, or add flags. For example, `ruralz control restore --prepare --data-dir PATH` generates the new online key encrypted under the key-encryption key and prints its public half for offline root signing. Then `ruralz control restore FILE --data-dir PATH --anchor-set PATH --backup-key-file PATH [--revocation-list PATH]`. Name where the backup encryption key comes from, or add an Open question owned by control-plane-and-gitops.

blocking.section: CLI command tree
blocking.issue: The document uses `ruralz bundle render --api-version` as the apiVersion migration tool, but render merges one overlay and substitutes `${VAR}`: without `--env`, values come from the process environment, and unset variables without a default are RZ-CFG-010. Its output is a one-file rendered Bundle that cannot replace a source tree with `overlays/<env>/` and `${VAR}` expressions. The OQ-configuration-model-7 decision rests on the claim that only comments are lost and that "its diff is empty by construction". That holds only for a rendered Bundle, not for migrating sources.
blocking.evidence: "| `ruralz bundle render` | Render for one Environment into a one-file Bundle; ... `--api-version` converts |" and "`ruralz bundle render --api-version ruralz/v1beta1` drops comments. For OQ-configuration-model-7 this document chooses option (a), accept the loss: conversion is rare, its diff is empty by construction"
blocking.fix: Specify that `--api-version` switches render into a source-conversion mode. In that mode it converts each base and overlay file in place (with `--output-dir DIR`), skips overlay merge and `${VAR}` substitution, and keeps file layout. Verify the result by rendering both trees for every Environment in `--environments` and requiring an empty `ruralz bundle diff`. blocking.section: Output formats and exit codes
blocking.issue: A CI job running `ruralz rollout status --wait` can hang forever, and the exit contract has no outcome for `paused`. `--wait` polls until the Rollout is terminal. `paused` is not terminal (pack 8.3), and every failure under `autoRollback: false` enters `paused` and waits for a human. `--timeout` has no default, and the exit code table maps only `complete`, `rolled-back`/`failed` and timeout. An operator writing a pipeline cannot tell what the command does when a gate fails.
blocking.evidence: Rollout, promotion and Node verbs: "`ruralz rollout status --wait` polls until the Rollout is terminal." Command table: "`--wait`, `--timeout DURATION`" (no default). Exit codes: "0 ... `rollout status --wait` reached `complete`"; "1 ... `rollout status --wait` ended in `rolled-back` or `failed`"; "2 ... `--wait` timeout".
blocking.fix: Define `--wait` as returning when the Rollout reaches a terminal state or `paused`. Give `paused` an exit code (1 with the pause reason in JSON, or a dedicated code such as 3, 'needs operator action'). Give `--timeout` a documented default. Add both to the exit code table and the Rollout verbs paragraph.

blocking.section: CLI command tree
blocking.issue: The worked example, the main CI recipe for operators, fails as written. (1) It omits `--control` and `--token-file`, but the document says scripts must pass those flags. (2) `ruralz bundle diff` exits 1 whenever there are changes, which is every non-empty pull request, so a CI shell run with `-e` (the default in common CI runners) fails every such job. (3) The post-merge `ruralz rollout approve` step appears in a script, but approvals require step-up TOTP, and without a terminal the CLI fails with exit 2.
blocking.evidence: Worked example: "ruralz bundle diff rev-162af81f5de4 ./bundle --env prod --environments control/environments.yaml --output json" and "ruralz rollout approve --env prod --digest sha256:..." / "ruralz rollout status prod-eu-west --wait --timeout 30m" with no `--control`/`--token-file`. Global flags: "until then scripts pass flags". Exit codes: "1 ... Diff with changes". REST API auth: "When the REST API demands step-up, the CLI prompts for a TOTP code on a terminal and otherwise fails with exit code 2".
blocking.fix: Add `--control https://control.shop.example:8090 --token-file ...` to every networked line. Tolerate exit 1 from diff explicitly (for example `|| test $? -eq 1`), with a one-line comment. Mark the approve and status lines as run by a human approver at a terminal, not in the pipeline, citing OQ-cli-and-api-surface-5.

blocking.section: CLI command tree
blocking.issue: The CLI accepts the display form `rev-<12 hex>` as a Revision lookup key and promises exit 2 on ambiguity. No REST operation can resolve a prefix: paths take only full digests, and `/api/v1/revisions` defines no filter or query parameter. A contributor cannot implement the lookup, yet the worked example depends on it.
blocking.evidence: Bundle verbs in detail: "Read commands accept the display form `rev-<12 hex>` as a lookup key and fail with exit code 2 when it is ambiguous". REST conventions: "Digests in paths and bodies are full `sha256:<64 hex>` values". REST table row `/api/v1/revisions`, `/api/v1/revisions/{digest}`: no query parameters.
blocking.fix: Add a lookup to the REST proposal, such as `GET /api/v1/revisions?prefix=<12 hex>&environment=NAME` returning every match with full digests. The CLI resolves through it and exits 2 on more than one match. Alternatively, state that only full digests are accepted and change the worked example.

h2s: Pros and cons of the options

blocking.section: Distributed state catalog
blocking.issue: The hot-key rule cannot hold as written. Every locally admitted request still runs GCRA, and the healthy derived ceiling is 2 x `requests` / N_published per Node, so a key sends up to N x ceiling = 2 x `requests` calls per window to its shard, and more while the count lags. At the stated 50% threshold, a key just under the threshold may therefore use 100% of a shard's about 100,000 calls per second (hypothesis). That contradicts CE-12's pass criteria (shard script CPU under 70%, no co-tenant breaker opens) and the 62.5% per-shard assumption in Cell sizing. The MUST also has no mechanism behind it. It relies on 'local-only enforcement (OQ-traffic-management-and-resilience-1)', which is only option (c) of that question, while its owner recommends option (a) (`config.perNodeCeiling`, `config.burst`), which does not stop GCRA per admitted request. A local-only mode also departs from pack 8.8 ('each locally admitted request runs GCRA'), yet OQ-scalability-and-distributed-state-11 does not list it among the pack 8.8 amendments.
blocking.evidence: Line 293: "Every locally admitted request still runs GCRA, so calls are at least the admitted rate, and no ceiling cuts them below the limit. A key whose `requests` per second exceeds 50% of one shard's calls, about 50,000 per second (hypothesis), MUST use local-only enforcement (OQ-traffic-management-and-resilience-1)". Line 607: "| CE-12 | Hot key at 10 times one shard's capacity, about 1,000,000 calls per second (hypothesis) | Calls at most N × ceiling per window; shard script CPU under 70% (target); no co-tenant breaker opens |". Traffic management Per-Node ceiling: "min(`requests`, max(10, ceil(2 × `requests` / N_published)))". Traffic management OQ-traffic-management-and-resilience-1: "(a) `config.perNodeCeiling`, `config.burst` (recommended); (b) a headroom multiplier; (c) `localOnly` mode". Worked case: `requests: 49000` per `1s` on 100 Nodes gives a ceiling of 980, so the key can send 98,000 GCRA calls per second, 98% of one shard (hypothesis).
blocking.fix: Derive the threshold from the call bound. Calls reach at most 2 x `requests` x N_serving / N_published, so a key MUST go local-only when 2 x `requests` exceeds 70% of one shard's calls: about 35,000 per second at steady state, or 25% (about 25,000 per second, hypothesis) to leave margin for count lag. Apply the same figure in the hot-key row of Cell and Cluster bottlenecks, in OQ-scalability-and-distributed-state-15 and in CE-12, whose tested key limit must sit below it. State that the MUST needs option (c) of OQ-traffic-management-and-resilience-1 (a `localOnly` mode), alone or alongside (a). Add that pack 8.8 amendment, with its fail-open and healthy bound of N_serving x ceiling per window (target), to OQ-scalability-and-distributed-state-11 and to the bounds table.

blocking.section: Stateless data plane
blocking.issue: The Quota denial cache has no size ceiling. Its only bound is a TTL, and neither this document nor Traffic management puts it inside the shared 1,048,576-entry key table. The number of entries therefore grows with the number of distinct exhausted keys seen in 60 s, which breaks SG-7 ('Every per-Node structure has a ceiling') and leaves an unbounded-memory path. A custom `config.key`, for example one that includes `source.ip`, multiplies the number of distinct keys.
blocking.evidence: Line 69: "| Quota denial cache | 60 s per key (target) | Next Quota script | The counter is re-read |". Line 42: "| SG-7 | Every per-Node structure has a ceiling, and every accuracy bound is a tagged number | P10 |". Traffic management Quotas: "Nodes cache the denial, keyed with the limit, up to 60 s (target)". Traffic management says only rate-limit "Buckets, local-only and over-limit entries share a Node-wide 1,048,576 entries", and the Quota denial cache is not among them.
blocking.fix: Give the row an entry bound. Either place Quota denials in the shared CLOCK-evicted key table ('shares the 1,048,576-entry table (target)') or give them their own segment, for example 65,536 entries (target), with CLOCK eviction. State why eviction is safe: an evicted denial only costs one more Quota script. Add the segment to the Per-Node limits table and to the memory sum under it.

non_blocking.suggestion: Line 355 (local-only row under OQ-traffic-management-and-resilience-20 (a)) uses the healthy, floored ceiling min(`requests`, max(10, ...)). Show the worked number: 10 per `1s` on 100 Nodes admits up to 1,000 per second, 100 x the limit, for the 10 s entry lifetime (hypothesis). Readers otherwise assume the fail-open, unfloored figure.

The pass criterion 'the published count drops at most 10% (target)' in CE-7 and CE-10 holds only under OQ-scalability-and-distributed-state-14 (a). Control plane and GitOps currently says 'large decreases publish at once' and counts only streams connected for 10 minutes. Mark both criteria 'under OQ-scalability-and-distributed-state-14 (a)'.

State client in-flight calls count 'until its reply or a connection reset'. State which read or write deadline resets a black-holed pipelined connection (for example a rueidis connection timeout, once the research file covers it). Otherwise the size of the stuck-call leak toward the 8,192 ceiling depends on TCP keepalive.

The roughly 470 MiB sum leaves out byte bounds for the Response Cache revalidation queue (256 saved requests, each with headers of up to 256 KiB, about 64 MiB worst case), the 8,192-span queue and `/tap` buffers. Add byte caps, or say that the sum covers only the listed rows.

'First-seen budget, Plugin key-rate and Semantic Cache concurrency counters | One counter each' understates the state. Plugin key-rate is per Policy, and if '10,000 keys per Policy per Node per minute' counts distinct keys it needs a set of up to 10,000 x 256 bytes per Policy. State the bound.
Line 163 tags '5,000 streams each' as (target) through the trailing tag, while Control plane and GitOps and line 585 give it as (hypothesis). Tag it (hypothesis) on line 163 as well.

Figure 3 has no branch for the local-only entry that option (a) of OQ-traffic-management-and-resilience-20 would add (admit with no GCRA call). Add an 'alt local-only entry (proposed)' branch, or say in the caption that the figure shows the conforming option (c).

Persisting the Node count under `${RURALZ_DATA_DIR}` (OQ-traffic-management-and-resilience-19 (c)) also changes the P4 wording in Vision and positioning ('no durable state beyond ...'). Name P4 in OQ-scalability-and-distributed-state-11 next to pack 8.11.
Make the Drain rule include the post-commit flush of up to 5 s (target): `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` MUST exceed preStop plus drain deadline plus flush.

blocking.section: Stateless data plane
blocking.issue: Acceptance criterion 3 still fails. The earlier finding is resolved for this document and its depends_on files: the State client, telemetry, `/tap`, AI candidate, first-seen, Plugin key-rate and Semantic Cache counter rows are all present. The table still calls itself 'the complete inventory', but it leaves out per-Node in-memory state that sibling architecture documents define. For one of these items, losing it is not safe. Security and identity keeps the signed revocation list in memory only, and a detached restart forgets it. A Node restarted during a Ruralz Control outage therefore accepts revoked JWTs, API keys and `auth.basic` usernames again. That makes the closing sentence ('the worst outcome is an over-charged Quota or Token Budget and a few extra admissions per key') and SG-3 wrong. Other items are missing: the `auth.basic` success cache and username throttle buckets, where a restart refuses legitimate clients with RZ-AUTH-007 for 25 to 50 s; the per-Node trace-sampling token buckets (Observability); the 32 MiB automatic-persisted-query cache (Multi-protocol); and the event-ingress fetch buffers and uncommitted offsets (Multi-protocol), where a crash causes redelivery, so an Upstream can see a message twice. An operator reading this table cannot predict these restart effects, and the security effect is the most serious one.
blocking.evidence: Line 50: "This table is the complete inventory of in-memory per-Node state; new per-Node state needs a row here before it ships." Line 76: "So a Node can be killed at any instant: the worst outcome is an over-charged Quota or Token Budget and a few extra admissions per key." Line 39 (SG-3): "Losing a Node loses only its in-flight requests, connections and the state [Stateless data plane] lists". Security and identity, Revocation: "Ruralz Control delivers one signed revocation list to every Node of a Cluster, checked in memory" and "**Persistence.** A detached restart forgets entries (OQ-security-and-identity-5)". Security and identity, auth.basic Ramp: "A restart or Zero-Downtime Upgrade starts with an empty cache and LRU ... callers beyond the queue get RZ-AUTH-007 with `Retry-After` meanwhile". Observability: "Two per-Node token buckets admit sampled traces (target)". Multi-protocol: "Automatic persisted queries | Disposable Node-local cache bounded by bytes (P4) ... | 32 MiB per Node (target)" and "Consumer group; commit after settle".
blocking.fix: Add rows, each with a Bound, a Rebuilt from and a Why losing it is safe entry. (1) Revocation list: bound one signed list; rebuilt from the Control Stream, or from the watched entry file in file mode. The safety cell must state the gap honestly: "Not safe while detached: a restarted detached Node forgets revocations until Ruralz Control returns (OQ-security-and-identity-5); Planned (M2)". (2) `auth.basic` success cache and username buckets: 10,000 and 100,000 entries (target); rebuilt by re-verification at the hash rate; safe because no credential is admitted without a hash, but expect a ramp of 25 to 50 s (hypothesis) with RZ-AUTH-007 refusals. (3) Trace-sampling buckets: two per Node; refilled at start; at worst one burst of extra sampled traces. (4) Automatic persisted query cache: 32 MiB (target); rebuilt when clients re-register; clients retry with the full document. (5) Event-ingress fetch buffers and uncommitted offsets or unacked messages: bounded by `maxBufferedBytes`; rebuilt by broker redelivery; at-least-once delivery, so an Upstream may see a message twice. Then rewrite line 76 as: "the worst outcomes are an over-charged Quota or Token Budget, a few extra admissions per key, a re-verification ramp for `auth.basic`, redelivered ingress messages and, while detached, forgotten revocations (OQ-security-and-identity-5)". Also align SG-3.

blocking.section: High availability > Ruralz Control availability; Distributed state catalog (Published Node count row); Chaos experiments (CE-7, CE-10)
blocking.issue: This is a regression from the L4X-2 fix. The new rule lets the published Node count fall when a qualified Node misses three heartbeats. Heartbeats run every 15 s (target), so the rule fires after about 45 s. After every replica restarts, or after a replica or the leader is lost, Nodes redial with full-jitter backoff up to 60 s. Per-replica stream admission also sheds them, and CE-10 itself allows 5 minutes to reconnect. Many qualified Nodes are therefore silent for more than three heartbeat intervals only because Ruralz Control restarted. The rule lowers the count anyway ('large decreases publish at once'), which is the collapse the fix was meant to prevent. CE-10's 'drops at most 10%' criterion cannot pass as the mechanism is specified. The text also never says when the missed-heartbeat clock starts for a replica that has just restarted with no heartbeat aggregates, which are held in memory and rebuilt by resync.
blocking.evidence: Line 179: "Only qualified Nodes missing three heartbeats may lower it, with qualification keyed by `node.id` in committed state". 04 line 376: "Nodes heartbeat every 15 s (target)". 04 line 385: "Backoff with full jitter, base 1 s, cap 60 s (target)." 04 line 383: "A per-replica token bucket on new streams answers excess with `Reconnect` or `RZ-CP-010`." 04 line 484: "Heartbeat aggregates, stream state | Memory; rebuilt by resync". Line 605: "| CE-10 | Every Ruralz Control replica restarted at once | All Nodes reconnect within 5 minutes (target); the published count drops at most 10% (target)".
blocking.fix: Failure scenario: 10,000 Nodes, and all three replicas restart. With the 60 s backoff cap and stream shedding, about half of the Nodes reconnect after more than 45 s. Each is counted as missing three heartbeats, so the count drops about 50% at once and derived ceilings double. Hot keys reach GCRA twice as often, and CE-10 fails. Fix: (1) At line 179, state that the missed-heartbeat clock starts only after a replica has been up and not stale for a reconnect grace of 5 minutes (target), matching CE-10. Before that, no decrease caused by missed heartbeats publishes. The replica loss and leader failover cases (CE-7) get the same rule. (2) Put the same grace in the catalog row and in option (a) of OQ-scalability-and-distributed-state-14. (3) The word band has only about 15 words of room (6,485 of 6,500 words), so condense other prose to make space, without removing text that resolved earlier findings.

blocking.section: Horizontal scaling > Autoscaling signals; High availability > Ruralz Control availability; Multi-region > Topologies (Home Region loss); Chaos experiments (CE-17)
blocking.issue: The L4X-1 fix added capacity that has to exist before a failure: pre-provisioning for R / (R − 1) of each Region's peak share, plus 30% headroom above peak for a Ruralz Control outage. The autoscaling rule in the same document removes that capacity. Scale-in happens when every signal is under half its threshold, and nothing sets an autoscaler minimum at the pre-provisioned count. When the home Region or Ruralz Control is lost, new Nodes cannot enroll, so capacity removed by scale-in cannot come back. This hidden single point of failure makes CE-17 depend on the autoscaler being off.
blocking.evidence: Line 141: "Scale out on the first signal over its threshold; scale in only when all are under half of it." Line 145: "80% × (Z − 1) / Z over 2 minutes for Z zones: 40% at two, 53% at three". Line 392: "each active-active Region SHOULD be pre-provisioned for R / (R − 1) times its peak share (target): 100% of global peak each with two Regions". Line 181: "autoscaling adds nothing during a long outage; Clusters SHOULD keep 30% headroom above peak (target)". Line 612: "| CE-17 | Home Region lost with every voter | The surviving Region serves full peak on pre-provisioned Nodes (target)".
blocking.fix: Failure scenario: two Regions with three zones each. Each Region is pre-provisioned to carry 100% of global peak, so at its own 50% peak share it runs at about half the CPU that full load would give, about 26% against the 53% threshold. All signals are under half their thresholds (26.5% CPU), so the autoscaler scales in and removes the Region-loss capacity every day. The home Region is then lost. Enrollment stops (`RZ-CP-004`), autoscaled replacements stay not ready, and the survivor runs at about 2x its CPU with in-flight units saturated, returning 503 `RZ-RT-005`. Fix: (1) Add to Autoscaling signals: "Autoscaler minimums MUST hold the pre-provisioned and headroom Node count (target); scale-in never goes below it." (2) Run CE-17 with the autoscaler enabled, after an off-peak scale-in period.

blocking.section: CLI command tree
blocking.issue: The replica join flow cannot work in the order this document gives. `ruralz control join` runs before `ruralz control serve`, so nothing on the new host answers Raft traffic on 8092 when the leader handles `Join`. Control plane and GitOps says the leader "signs the replica's certificate and adds a voter" in that same step. With hashicorp/raft, adding a voter that is not running raises the quorum at once. On the common 1-to-3 bootstrap, a 1-voter cluster becomes 2 voters with one down: the leader loses its lease and writes, logins and Enrollment stop (RZ-CP-004) until `serve` starts. The command also has no flag for the new replica's own advertised peer address (HOST:8092). The leader needs that address to add the server, and the peer certificate needs it as a SAN for mTLS on 8092. Finally, the document does not say how `ruralz control serve` on a data directory written by `join` knows not to bootstrap a new cluster and generate new CAs, which is what it does on an empty Control Store.
blocking.evidence: "`ruralz control join` runs on the new replica's host before `ruralz control serve`. It generates the key pair in `--data-dir`, dials `--peer` pinned to the SHA-256 fingerprint of the 8092 server CA ... then writes the certificate chain and peer CA beside the key"; command row: "| `ruralz control join` | Join a new replica to Raft | `--data-dir PATH`, `--peer HOST:8092`, `--join-token-file PATH` |"; Control plane and GitOps: "`ruralz control serve` on an empty Control Store generates the CAs or loads supplied ones; `ruralz control join` redeems a one-time `admin` token in `Join`, and the leader signs the replica's certificate and adds a voter."
blocking.fix: Add `--advertise HOST:8092` (required) to `ruralz control join`, and put that address into the certificate request as a SAN. State that `Join` only issues the certificate and records a pending member. The replica is added as a non-voter only when `ruralz control serve` on that data directory first connects over 8092 with its new peer certificate. It is promoted to voter only after it catches up to the leader's commit index (hashicorp/raft AddNonvoter, then AddVoter). State that `serve` on a joined data directory never bootstraps or generates CAs. Record the voter-timing change as a proposal to Control plane and GitOps, in OQ-cli-and-api-surface-9 or a new Open question owned by control-plane-and-gitops. The other option is to make join a mode of serve (`ruralz control serve -- --join HOST:8092 --join-token-file PATH --advertise HOST:8092`), so the replica is running before it becomes a member.

blocking.section: CLI command tree
blocking.issue: `ruralz control restore` does not say what happens to Raft membership. A Raft snapshot carries the old cluster configuration: the old voters' IDs and addresses. Restored into an empty deployment on new hosts, that configuration leaves the new replica waiting for voters that no longer exist. It never elects a leader, so it can never open the higher `storeEpoch`. Neither restore step takes the local replica's advertised peer address, and neither step resets membership.
blocking.evidence: "2. `FILE --data-dir PATH --anchor-set PATH --backup-key-file PATH` verifies and decrypts the backup, requires a root-signed anchor set holding the prepared key, and opens a higher `storeEpoch` before any delivery."; Control plane and GitOps: "`ruralz control backup` writes a Raft snapshot plus referenced content, consistent at one index"
blocking.fix: Add `--advertise HOST:8092` (required) to step 2. State that restore replaces the snapshot's Raft configuration with a single voter: the local replica at that address, with a new server ID, as hashicorp/raft RecoverCluster does. It also clears old peer certificates from the trust set. Other replicas then join with `ruralz control join` (L1-1). If the Control plane document should own this, add it to OQ-cli-and-api-surface-9, or open a new Open question owned by control-plane-and-gitops.

blocking.section: Memory budget
blocking.issue: The memory decomposition cannot meet PB-6 as written. 95 MiB is 99,614,720 bytes. That leaves 385,280 bytes of the 100,000,000-byte base, but the table puts 2 MiB (2,097,152 bytes) of sharded label sets 'inside the base'. At R = 1,000 the PB-6 allowance is 102,000,000 bytes. The idle base, the sharded label sets and the 2 MB snapshot from the reload table add up to about 103.7 MB, so PB-6 fails by construction. The 2 KB per-Route slope is also used up by the snapshot alone (2 MB per 1,000 Routes, 34 MB per 17,000). Nothing is left for unsharded label sets, which Observability costs at 300 bytes per histogram label set plus 120 bytes per counter series. Nothing is left either for heap-goal retention at GOGC=100.
blocking.evidence: "| Idle RSS, no Revision, telemetry at defaults | 95 MiB or less (target) |"; "| Sharded label sets of the first 1,000 admitted Routes | 2 MiB or less at 4 stripes (target), inside the base |"; "PB-6 compares bytes: 100,000,000 plus 2,000 per Route (target)."; "| Per-Route slope between 1,000 and 17,000 Routes | 2 KB or less (target) | Router entries, chain arrays, CEL programs and unsharded label sets"; reload table "| 1,000 (1,151) | ... | 2 MB or less (target) | 8 MB or less (target) |"
blocking.fix: Publish one decomposition whose sums close, and show the arithmetic at R = 0, 1,000 and 17,000. One way: set idle RSS to 92 MiB or less (target) and update OQ-performance-budgets-and-benchmarking-5 to match. Keep the sharded label sets inside the base. Split the per-Route slope into snapshot, 1.5 KB or less (target), and unsharded label sets, 0.5 KB or less (target), and change the snapshot-size column to match. Then state how RSS at idle settle accounts for GOGC=100 retention: either measure the slope on live heap with an RSS retention factor (hypothesis), or budget the RSS slope at twice live bytes. blocking.section: Budget philosophy (Budget catalog and SLO ties); Benchmark suite and CI gating (Constants the suite verifies)
blocking.issue: O1 cannot exercise PB-11 or the in-flight ceiling. O1 is S1, which uses 256 HTTP/1.1 keep-alive connections, so at most 256 requests can be in flight and the 20,000-unit ceiling is never reached. RZ-RT-005 never fires, and excess load waits in the generator. That breaks the 0.5% run-validity rule, and O1 is not exempted from it. With enough connections, Little's law gives about 400 ms of queueing before the first rejection. blocking.section: Decision outcome (HTTP/3 row) and Decision drivers
blocking.issue: The HTTP/3 path has no resource bounds. The drivers promise per-connection stream, buffer and frame limits 'as the data plane's Bounded resources table fixes them', but every ceiling in the ADR and in that table is an HTTP2Config or net.Listener mechanism, and none of them reaches quic-go. The Node connection ceiling is 'a counting net.Listener [that] stops calling Accept', which cannot count QUIC connections on a UDP socket. quic-go's incoming-stream count and connection and stream flow-control windows are quic.Config settings; to my knowledge they default to 100 streams and receive windows that auto-tune into megabytes. quic-go's http3.Server also keeps its own header limit, separate from the 256 KiB Server.MaxHeaderBytes. On top of that, no research shows that quic-go's ResponseWriter honors http.ResponseController read and write deadlines, and the Deadlines row and the data plane's retirement protocol depend on them. As written, one HTTP/3 connection can hold far more than the 592 KiB (hypothesis) the data plane budgets per connection, and the roughly 19 GiB worst-case Node sum does not hold. That contradicts System overview's 'Bounded everything' principle.
blocking.evidence: "**Bounded resources**: per-connection stream, buffer and frame limits and per-request deadlines, as the data plane's [Bounded resources](../architecture/03-data-plane.md#bounded-resources) table fixes them." and "| HTTP/3 | quic-go `http3` v0.63.x, pinned, on UDP at the `https` listener's port when `http3: true`, with the same Routes, Policies and certificates, behind an internal interface; a build constraint keeps it out of FIPS builds (OQ-tech-stack-and-libraries-9) | Planned (M3) |"; data plane: "Client connections per Node | 20,000 connections (target); a counting `net.Listener` stops calling `Accept` at the ceiling"

blocking.section: Decision outcome (Upstream layer row)
blocking.issue: The row does not say whether HTTP2Config.StrictMaxConcurrentRequests is true or false, and 'honoring server limits' implies true. The research defines the field as 'whether to open a new connection when an existing one hits its stream limit'. If it is true, an Endpoint gets no second connection. blocking.section: Decision outcome (Consensus row, Figure 2), Consequences, Confirmation (Fencing test)
blocking.issue: The fencing argument confuses Raft commit with state-machine acceptance, so the safety claim is false and the Confirmation test cannot be built as written. In hashicorp/raft every entry that reaches a voter quorum commits. The FSM only decides whether to accept it, and `ApplyFuture.Response()` returns that verdict. A deposed leader's entry can also commit later. Example: leader L1 proposes assignment A at sequence n+1, replicates it to follower F, then is partitioned. F wins the election with A in its log and signs its own assignment B at n+1. A precedes B in the log, so A commits and applies and B is rejected, although B is also committed. Two consequences follow. (1) 'replicas serve Nodes only committed entries' would let a replica deliver B, which carries a valid leader signature at (storeEpoch, n+1). The Node-side highest-pair check cannot tell A from B, so two Nodes could activate different assignments at the same sequence. Only state the FSM accepted may be served. (2) A new leader that signs its next sequence before its FSM has applied the entries from earlier terms is rejected on every proposal. The design needs the leader services to start after `raft.Barrier()` on election, and it needs a rule that a proposal whose FSM response is a rejection is re-read and re-signed. blocking.section: Decision outcome (ACK/NACK row, Reconnect row, Figure 2)
blocking.issue: An ACK can be lost, and the ADR has no way to recover it. The rules tie an ACK to one per-stream nonce. The stream can break after the Node activates but before its Ack reaches the Raft ACK bitmap: a replica crashes holding forwarded Acks, a leader fails over inside the 250 ms bitmap commit window, or the follower queue drops entries. When the Node reconnects, its Hello shows active digest equal to the assigned digest, so Figure 2 sends nothing and no Ack is ever produced. The Rollout engine then waits out the ACK timeout and retries, and the Node is quarantined as lagging even though it runs the right Revision. A replica or leader failure during a batch can therefore push the lagging count past max(1, 5% of the batch) and roll back or pause a healthy Rollout.
blocking.evidence: ACK/NACK row: "Every configuration message carries a `nonce`; `Ack` means active, not durable; `Nack` keeps the active Revision and carries `code` and `class`; stale nonces are ignored". Figure 2: `same{"Active digest equals the assigned digest?"}` -> `none["Send nothing, HeartbeatReply carries the promotion"]`. Owning document, Replica roles: "Followers forward `Ack` and `Nack` at once and heartbeat aggregates every 5 s (target) through a bounded queue that drops the oldest"; Rollout plan: "ACKs commit as bitmaps every 250 ms (target)".
blocking.fix: Make the ACK record level-triggered, the same way Last-Known-Good promotion already is. Add to the ACK/NACK row: "Ruralz Control records an ACK per (`node.id`, `storeEpoch`, `assignmentSeq`), not per stream. A `Hello` or `Heartbeat` whose active digest, `storeEpoch` and `assignmentSeq` match the Node's pending assignment counts as its `Ack`, so a lost `Ack` never makes a Node lag." Label Figure 2's 'Send nothing' branch as recording the implicit ACK. Add a container-free test to Confirmation: kill the replica holding a forwarded Ack before the bitmap commit, and the Node is still counted ACKed after it reconnects.

The Figure 2 tree picks the transport only from the size of the change from the active digest. The retry is therefore the same Delta, which fails the same way until the Node is quarantined. The fixed point is G = (4 vCPU - 60,000 x 16 us) / (100 us - 16 us), about 36,190 rps, which is 90.5% of saturation, not 92%. That leaves 0.5 points of margin. (2) The 16 us is the rejection's p50, but CPU is consumed at the mean. The p99 is 40 us, so the mean is likely above p50. At an 18 us mean, G is about 35,610 rps (89%), which fails PB-11. blocking.section: Decision outcome (rules table, row Time); Confirmation
blocking.issue: The Time rule says wazero enforces limits.timeout as a plain per-call context deadline. The owning document requires that the call timer stop while the guest is parked in its one State Store call. A context deadline cannot be paused. In wazero, WithCloseOnContextDone starts a watcher goroutine per Call that closes the module when ctx.Done() fires, and the same ctx reaches Host Functions. If the rule is built as written with context.WithTimeout, a parked state.* call is killed at 5 ms and its instance is closed. During a State Store brownout (50 ms stateStoreTimeout in the owning document's Sizing table), every parked instance then becomes RZ-PLG-002 and is discarded. That produces the refill storm and fault-breaker trip the parked-bound design exists to prevent, and it contradicts the owning document's Default limits row.
blocking.evidence: ADR Time row: "`WithCloseOnContextDone(true)` with a per-call deadline from `limits.timeout`, default 5 ms (target)". Owning document, Default limits: "Wall-clock time per call (`limits.timeout`) | 5 ms (target) | Stopped while parked"; Runtime rule 7: "During its one State Store call the guest is parked, timer stopped".
blocking.fix: Reword the Time row to name a mechanism that can pause: "`WithCloseOnContextDone(true)` on a cancel-only per-call context (context.WithCancel of the request context); a host timer of `limits.timeout` cancels it, is stopped while the guest is parked in its State Store call and resumes with the remaining time; the State Store call uses its own `stateStoreTimeout` context (pack section 8.7)". Add a Confirmation limit case to the Plugin ABI conformance bullet: a parked `state_get` that lasts longer than `limits.timeout` returns to the guest without RZ-PLG-002, and the same guest then looping past the remaining time gets RZ-PLG-002.

blocking.section: Decision outcome (rules table, row Memory); Consequences
blocking.issue: The Memory row fixes only the page cap. It does not choose the linear-memory backing store, so the claim that Gateway limits.maxPluginMemoryBytes caps the Node cannot be shown to hold for process memory. With wazero defaults, linear memory is a Go-heap byte slice that grows by reallocation and copy. Each memory.grow briefly holds both the old and the new slice, and the old one stays as garbage until the next GC. Because this memory is live Go heap, it also raises the GOGC heap target: 2 GiB of Plugin memory can push the heap target to about 4 GiB under GOGC=100. Resident memory can therefore exceed the Node cap by up to 2x, which breaks the owning document's "Full reservation makes the Node cap a hard bound" rule and P6's "never crashes the Node" under a container memory limit. Research section 2.2 names the two wazero knobs that decide this (WithMemoryCapacityFromMax and experimental.MemoryAllocator), but the ADR mentions neither.
blocking.evidence: ADR Memory row: "`WithMemoryLimitPages` from `limits.memoryBytes`, default 16 MiB (target), replacing wazero's 65536-page (4 GiB) default ([source](https://github.com/wazero/wazero/blob/main/config.go)); Gateway `limits.maxPluginMemoryBytes` caps the Node". Research go-libraries-runtime.md section 2.2: "`WithMemoryCapacityFromMax(true)` allocates the maximum eagerly" and "`experimental.MemoryAllocator` lets the host supply the `LinearMemory` backing store".
blocking.fix: In the Memory row, choose and cite one backing store (research URLs config.go and experimental/memory.go). Either use `WithMemoryCapacityFromMax(true)`, which allocates eagerly, matches full reservation and avoids reallocation copies, or use an `experimental.MemoryAllocator` that reserves `limits.memoryBytes` outside the Go heap. State how the Node sets GOMEMLIMIT relative to maxPluginMemoryBytes. If the choice needs a benchmark first, add it to OQ-wasm-plugin-system-16 and add a Bad consequence for the resident-memory overhead (hypothesis). Add a Confirmation test: at the Node cap, with instances growing to their limit, resident memory stays within the cap plus the stated headroom (target).

non_blocking.section: Decision outcome (rows Runtimes and cache, Compilation); Consequences
non_blocking.suggestion: In wazero main, a module's cache ID hashes the Wasm bytes, the listeners and the ensure-termination flag, not the memory limit (internal/wasm/module.go AssignModuleID). A shared NewCompilationCache engine keeps compiled modules reference-counted and frees them when the last CompiledModule.Close runs (internal/engine/wazevo/engine.go DeleteCompiledModule). blocking.section: Decision outcome (rules table, rows State Store and Capabilities)
blocking.issue: The per-request State Store budget cannot be met as written by an Upstream-scoped Plugin Policy. Data plane runs `onUpstreamRequest` "per leg attempt, including retries and steps", and Traffic management says "each retry reruns `onUpstreamRequest`". A Plugin that calls `state_get` in `onUpstreamRequest` spends its one call on the first attempt. On the retry the same call returns `ERR_BUDGET`, which this ADR makes sticky. Result: `RZ-PLG-006` under `failureMode` (default `closed`, so 503). A correct Plugin therefore fails on every retried request. Composition steps that share one Plugin Policy hit the same problem. With parallel `aggregate` steps it is worse: the per-request counter is contended between leg goroutines, so which leg fails is a race. Neither this ADR nor the owning document says how the budget applies across attempts and steps, and the ADR's checklist would freeze the sticky `ERR_BUDGET` rule.
blocking.evidence: ADR State Store row: "One blocking `state_get` or `state_incr` per Plugin Policy per request before commit, a second returning `ERR_BUDGET`". Capabilities row: "`ERR_PHASE`, `ERR_BUDGET` and `ERR_DENIED` are sticky and yield `RZ-PLG-006`". Data plane Phase table: "`onUpstreamRequest` | Per leg attempt, including retries and steps". Traffic management and resilience: "each retry reruns `onUpstreamRequest`".
blocking.fix: Add the missing rule and track it as an Open question without changing pack section 8.7. For example, add to the State Store row: "in upstream-leg Phases the host records the first `state_get` or `state_incr` result per Policy per request and replays it on later attempts and steps, with no round trip and no `ERR_BUDGET`; parallel steps serialize on that per-request slot". Alternatively, forbid `state.*` for Upstream-scoped Plugin Policies (RZ-CFG-020). Add a Bad consequence for this, and record the choice as a new OQ-wasm-plugin-system-20 in the owning document, cited under More information. Add a conformance case to Confirmation: an Upstream-scoped `state.read` Plugin on a Route with one retry and on a two-step `aggregate` composition gets no `RZ-PLG-006`.

blocking.section: Decision outcome (rules table, row Results; Figure 2)
blocking.issue: The Results row gives the output-buffer rule as universal: an output write above its capacity writes nothing and returns the full length. The owning document's Contract makes body and chunk reads an exception: they are offset reads that return the bytes written and 0 at the end. As written in the ADR, `request_body_read` and `response_body_read` on a body larger than the guest buffer write nothing, so the guest must allocate the whole body. With the default 16 MiB `limits.memoryBytes` (target), a body near that size, plus the copy that `*_body_replace` needs, cannot fit in linear memory. `memory.grow` then fails, the guest traps with `RZ-PLG-003`, and the only escape is a larger per-instance limit, which shrinks N in every pool. The review checklist freezes the "memory convention", so shipping this wording would make the streaming read impossible within v1.
blocking.evidence: ADR Results row: "Every Host Function returns `i32`, negative only for errors (`-1` ERR_ABSENT to `-7` ERR_DENIED); an output write above its capacity writes nothing and returns the full length". Owning document, Contract, row Output buffers: "Writes to `(o, c)` return the full length; above `c`, nothing was written and the guest retries. Body and chunk reads return bytes written, 0 at the end".
blocking.fix: Append this to the Results row: "except `request_body_read`, `response_body_read` and `chunk_read`, which take an offset (bodies) and return the bytes written, 0 at the end, so a guest streams a body through a fixed buffer". Mention in Figure 2's caption that the figure shows the header-read case only. Add to the conformance bullet a body larger than `limits.memoryBytes` that is read in fixed-size chunks without `RZ-PLG-003`.

blocking.section: Decision outcome (rules table, row proxy-wasm, Planned (M4)); Consequences (last Bad bullet)
blocking.issue: The adapter row claims the same host, limits, `RZ-PLG` codes and `failureMode`. Request affinity breaks two limits the native host relies on. First, the native pool gives each Phase call its own idle instance with a wait of at most 1 ms (target). A pinned proxy-wasm context instead waits for its one instance, which serializes calls for up to 1,000 contexts (target). One guest call running to its 5 ms `limits.timeout` (target) delays the Phase calls of up to 999 other requests, and no wait bound or error code is stated for this. Second, a trap discards the instance, so its fault radius is every pinned context, up to 1,000 in-flight requests (target), not one call. That contradicts "a faulty Plugin fails only its own Policy" at request granularity and the owning document's per-call fault model. The ADR also narrows OQ-wasm-plugin-system-17 to recycling, although the owning document asks about recycling and faults.
blocking.evidence: ADR adapter row: "Ruralz adapter on the same host, Capabilities, limits, `RZ-PLG` codes and `failureMode`". ADR Consequences: "the adapter pins each request to one instance, since proxy-wasm keeps stream state in guest memory: 1,000 contexts per instance (target), recycling open (OQ-wasm-plugin-system-17)". Owning document, Runtime rule 6: "Requests never compile or instantiate; they wait at most 1 ms (target)"; proxy-wasm stance: "calls are serialized; 1,000 contexts per instance (target) (OQ-wasm-plugin-system-17)"; OQ-wasm-plugin-system-17: "How does adapter pinning interact with recycling and faults?"
blocking.fix: Add to the adapter row: "a pinned call waits for its instance at most the pool wait, 1 ms (target), then fails with `RZ-PLG-005` under `failureMode`; a trap fails every context pinned to that instance, each under its own Policy's `failureMode`". Change the Consequences bullet to say "recycling and fault radius open (OQ-wasm-plugin-system-17)". Add a Planned (M4) adapter conformance case: one trapping context does not affect contexts on other instances, and pinned waits respect the bound.

non_blocking.suggestion: "admitting outbound calls would only add Host Functions within v1" understates the change. Pack section 8.7 rule 6 requires any remote call before commit to be declared on the Policy with a timeout and `failureMode`, and P3 requires the same. That needs a `Plugin` or `Policy` field that the Configuration model does not have. Reword as "would add Host Functions within v1 plus a declared timeout and `failureMode` per pack section 8.7 rule 6 (OQ-wasm-plugin-system-5)".
